scenes.headline: How a vector index skips the training step
scenes.sub: TurboVec: rotate, quantize, and search packed codes, in Rust.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Syrup! TurboVec is a Rust vector index that keeps pace with FAISS, with no training step at all. Here's how.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Product quantization learns its codebook from your data. TurboVec reshapes your data into a distribution whose best codebook is already known.

scenes.title: Encoding a vector, with nothing learned

items.say: Normalize each vector, keeping its length aside for scoring.

items.text: Rotate by a seeded random matrix
items.say: Rotate it by a random orthogonal matrix, built once from a seed.
A small shift and scale, fit once on the first batch, snaps real embeddings onto the ideal shape.
Quantize each coordinate with Lloyd-Max levels precomputed for that known shape.
Pack it into two, three or four bits, plus one correction number that keeps dot products unbiased.

scenes.title: Search runs on the packed codes

steps.say: A query arrives, and TurboVec builds a small lookup table for it.
Hand-written SIMD kernels score the packed codes directly, thirty-two vectors to a block, by table lookup. Nothing is decompressed.
A filter is a bitmask, checked inside the kernel. Blocks with nothing allowed are skipped.
So a filtered search returns the true top k, with no recall penalty and no over-fetch.

scenes.label: a 10-million-vector corpus, float32 versus TurboVec
scenes.note: recall matches or beats FAISS IndexPQ; 12-19% faster on ARM
scenes.say: A ten-million-vector corpus drops from thirty-one gigabytes to four. On the repo's benchmarks it mostly matches FAISS recall, and trails slightly in a few two-bit setups.

scenes.text: Reshape the data so the best codebook is known, and the training phase disappears: ingest online, never rebuild.

recap: Rotate, quantize with a fixed table, bit-pack
SIMD kernels score packed codes by lookup
A flat scan: millions of vectors, not billions
scenes.say: To recap: nothing to train, codes scored in place, and a flat index sized for millions.
